title: Conditional κ = 7.50237961741364·10⁻⁴: kernels, early restorations, terminal sinks, a post-sink retiming and addition reordering on the gen5b word (+0.473% over #296)
body:
# Conditional κ = 7.50237961741364·10⁻⁴: kernels, early restorations, terminal sinks, a post-sink retiming and addition reordering on the gen5b word (+0.473% over #296)

One self-contained package, `research/five-stage-gen5b-kernels-restorations-sinks/`, with its own workflow. No existing file is changed.

**κ = 187559490435341/(25·10¹⁶) = 7.50237961741364·10⁻⁴**: +0.473% over #296's gen5b word (7.46709720962478·10⁻⁴), +0.633% over #295, +0.822% over #287. (Earlier versions of this PR: 7.49899215319498·10⁻⁴ without the last two stages, 7.49920356821633·10⁻⁴ with the post-sink retiming.) Bit coarse 7.50462·10⁻⁴, complex coarse 7.54736·10⁻⁴ (#233's word); the bit side binds with a 0.57% margin — with #193's complex supplier (7.47455·10⁻⁴) this word would now be complex-bound.

## What it is

#296's package (the gen5b bit word: #285's generator and pair module with an exactly optimal alternative local design and a debt-10 all-but-one module; #287's descent and target squares re-derived; #233's complex supplier) with the three transcript stages of #290 and #295, each re-screened on gen5b and priced on the whole word (the φ-ledger model reproduces #296's κ exactly and predicted each row below exactly):

| stage (census on gen5b) | mechanism | φ | κ | gain |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| #296 base | — | — | 7.46709720962478·10⁻⁴ | — |
| **1,720 collective kernel entries** — 920 twin pairs (904 on a line, 16 on rank 3) and 800 families (375 quadruples, 425 triples); entrance rank 2,192 | #254/#259/#272 (Dugongue), stage of #282/#290 | −3,799.1 | 7.49121118627047·10⁻⁴ | +0.323% |
| **440 early helper restorations** (cut at record 757,526) | #280 (utcorvusvolat-dotcom), endpoint banking #283 | −886.6 | 7.49686102247225·10⁻⁴ | +0.075% |
| **7 terminal sinks** (R 15,434 → 15,427) | #283 (Dugongue) | −333.7 | 7.49899215319498·10⁻⁴ | +0.028% |
| **second concave-descent retiming after the sinks** — 113 gates (31 operand-chain frames, 34 constructed join/meet frames, 36 connected pair blocks), 77 new bases | #287/#291 (rohanarun), #286 (GamingPuzzled), #289 (gupt1156), #270 (utcorvusvolat-dotcom) | −33.3 | 7.49920356821633·10⁻⁴ | +0.003% |
| **addition reordering** (two rounds, 237 moves): a single addition moved past its sibling incidences into the frame of a neighbouring incidence — 213 root deliveries y += h from a rank-21 frame into y's next rank-22 frame, 22 forward gates from a rank-18 back to an earlier rank-16 frame, 2 more in round 2; exact over Z because no crossed gate reads its destination or writes its source | found while testing Khattar–Gidney's conditionally clean ancillae (arXiv:2407.17966), whose literal class is empty here | −496.6 | **7.50237961741364·10⁻⁴** | +0.042% |

gen5b is much richer in kernels than gen5: 952 twin pairs share a cut and a nondegenerate common line (292 on gen5); helper responses have F₂ rank 1,760 and nullity 11,440 over 13,200 plain helpers; with a common cut and entrance there are 952 pairs, 2,104 triples and 3,807 quadruples.

## Checks

`python3 -B verify.py` runs fifteen fresh stages — virtual, raw, bit (descent + targets), kernel, restore, sink, descent2, reorder, reorder2, scalar, primes, banks, complex, math, finite — with fifteen omitted-stage negative controls. The reorder stage re-derives every frozen move on the actual word (record content, the anchor frame's exact basis, the crossed-interval rule, disjoint operand sets), runs the F₂ replay of all columns forward and inverse, an omission control (932 wrong rows), an independent integer replay mod 2⁶¹ − 1 with random dirty inputs, the MOVE rebuild with both reflected ledgers, and #287/#291's exact source-span rule on every gate of its output. The post-sink retiming (`descent2_transform.py`, #287's transform with final frames read from the actual post-sink state so restored helpers keep their early endpoints) keeps every check of #287's descent (byte-identical scalar/COPY projection, nested chains with every MOVE rebuilt, fixed endpoints, COPY lifetimes, exact integer operand spans, nondegenerate frames, both reflected ledgers) and adds a forward and inverse F₂ replay; the deficit stays 4,400. Kernel: 38,036 compensation reads removed, 5,790 setup/restore gates, all columns forward and inverse, omission controls 3,190 / 1,438 wrong rows, prefix relation checked for every entry. Restore: 1,767,480 crossed-gate commutation checks, omission control 440 wrong rows, completion P_σ + I − P_E. Sinks: omission controls 28 / 21 / 21 wrong rows, each removed helper frees 24 rank, deficit re-checked at R = 15,427. Banks: literal stock 1,236,750 → 1,229,750, 807,350 banks, 910 exact charts, 3,954 entrances; the 1,574 residual-23 pivots are tiled as (r⁴, 24, 4²⁴⁻ʳ) — width 120 and full — because #283's (r⁴, 4³⁰⁻ʳ) rule runs out of rank-4 blocks on this word. Every changed literal is a recomputed pin; nothing is dropped. The two intermediate packages (kernel only; kernel + restore) also pass `verify.py` end to end.

## Verify

    python -m pip install -r research/five-stage-gen5b-kernels-restorations-sinks/requirements.txt    # sympy 1.14.0
    python3 -B research/five-stage-gen5b-kernels-restorations-sinks/verify.py --output /tmp/gen5b-krs-verification   # about 5 minutes; not under -I

The workflow runs it and the bit-word regeneration on Ubuntu.

## Scope and limits

* Conditional finite construction under the retained public all-size hypotheses (no Lean certificate for the bit side; the complex word is Lean-checked via #256). #285, #287 and #296 are open; inherited stages are reused unchanged.
* Not composed: #280's transported dirty entrances (almost no candidates once the target squares are in place), restorations whose join is the full frame (34), quintuple families (never net-positive), and the retiming rungs stacked on #290 (#291–#293), which were bound to the gen5 transcript.
* `KERNEL-PROOF.md` and `LEVERS-PROOF.md` describe the mechanisms with their gen5 counts (#290/#295); the README carries this word's counts.
